target_customer: Construction suppliers, distributors and subcontractors (credit and collections teams) that wait on slow, paperwork-heavy construction payments
problem: Construction payments are slow and buried in lien notices, waivers and compliance paperwork, so suppliers and independent workers wait long for money and carry credit risk.
business_model: B2B SaaS and payments: lien and notice management, automated waivers and integrated payments; early product paired software with a credit line

founders.name: Patrick Hogan
previous_startups: Tenfold (sold to LivePerson, per press release summary of the Series A announcement)

competitors.name: Levelset
competitors.what: New Orleans software for construction payment paperwork: notices, mechanics liens, bond claims, payment demands and lien waivers
competitors.funding_then: Series B of about 10M reported January 2018 by an aggregator (startupintros), lead not confirmed

technical_complexity.rationale: Lien and notice rules vary by state and waiver workflows, invoicing and later payments and credit add compliance and integration work; standard software with domain complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Deep supplier workflow integration and state-by-state compliance knowledge are harder to copy than a simple invoicing tool, but lien software rivals already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A directory entry reports Procore acquired Levelset in 2021 (single third-party source, unverified); Handle remained independent and raised a Series B in 2026.

market_need_then: Construction payment chains are long and compliance-heavy; at YC exit the company reported 22,800 dollars monthly revenue six weeks after launch (per a profile summary), and TechCrunch in March 2020 described workers waiting for checks to clear.

branding.domain_note: Company uses handle.com; a domain industry blog headline reports a handle.com sale for 180000 dollars, but the buyer and date were not verified.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B tone about getting paid and managing compliance

brand_strength.rationale: Press about the company covers funding and products; no source shows brand-driven awareness, mascot or community, though the exact .com helps credibility.

outcome_analysis: Handle started with lien rights and compliance for construction suppliers, reported early revenue after YC in 2019, then expanded into waivers, payments and credit. It raised a 10 million Series A in March 2022, strategic money from Amex Ventures and Suffolk Technologies in March 2024 and a 27 million Series B in May 2026, and now has about 200 employees and large distributor customers such as Ferguson and Cemex.
notes: The 4.5 million round has no date or investors in the TechCrunch article (March 2020 calls it known venture capital); Seedtable lists a seed in May 2019 with estimated allocations and Yespress dates it 2020, so the date is left null.
